detailed_description:
The target video is a bold screen-printed 1960s rock gig-poster illustration of a suburban home garage, a locked-off camera. Laws of this world: the camera holds one locked framing for the whole window, everyone fully in frame; everything on the cover is alive and moving, slow and subtle between the hits: the three bare bulbs glow and pulse slowly; their warm halos brighten and soften; the bulbs sway slightly on their cords; the shadows on the garage door panels shift slowly and softly; the amplifier grille catches the light; the cymbals shimmer softly; the strings vibrate; hands have five fingers resting on real instruments; each performer's motion stays in his own hands on his own instrument, each with his own small distinct touch; every person holds a calm, steady posture, heads calm, shoulders still, breathing and blinking softly, each head drifting slowly and slightly.
THE SINGER is the one singer and sings <Audio 1>: lips on each sung syllable (15 in this window, from 3.45 s), lips and jaw shaping each word, mouth opening moderately, restrained, both hands staying on the microphone, his head drifting slowly in small turns on held notes, shoulders still; between lines the lips rest together. Everyone else keeps lips together.
THE DRUMMER: on each drum hit (14 in this window, from 1.43 s) his right stick lands on the snare or his foot presses the kick pedal; on every first beat his right stick taps the cymbal; head calm, his motion in his hands and foot.
THE BASSIST: on each bass note (5, from 1.42 s) his right fingers pluck a string while his left hand stays on the neck; between notes his fingers keep a steady pulse on the strings; feet planted, head calm, shoulders still.
THE GUITARIST: on each new chord of the guitar part (15 in this window, from 0.07 s) his right hand strums down across the strings while his left hand holds the chord on the neck; feet planted beside the amplifier, head calm, shoulders still.
The world answers the music: on each drum hit (14 in this window) the three bulbs brighten a little and settle; on each snare the cymbals shimmer with light; with the bass notes the bulbs sway slowly on their cords; with the guitar chords the amplifier grille glows a little warmer.
The window builds gently: the hands play a little fuller bar by bar, the light and colours steady as on the cover.

a small suburban garage, a loud amplifier hum, the concrete room ringing.

a raw 1960s garage rock song, 132 bpm, about 5 bars in this window. The drums pounding, 14 hits, from 1.43 s. The electric bass, 5 notes, from 1.42 s, held and ringing. The fuzz electric guitar, 15 chord attacks, from 0.07 s. The voice sings 15 syllables, from 3.45 s.
